en: Abhidhānottaratantra, Chapter 37 [Tibetan & Sanskrit 40] = Lokesh Chandra facsimile edition = 1138 AD palm-leaf manuscript.
[129–132 are missing; likely the beginning of 133:
Now I shall further proclaim the characteristics of the ḍākinīs.
By means of which one may correctly understand the ḍākinīs who abide in the samaya.
But that woman who is reddish-white and emits the fragrance of a lotus, [is of that kind].
With a gentle gaze, she looked at each one with eyes full of passion.
For that woman whose nails and eyes are likewise blood-red, [she is not to be approached].
And in the house, a lotus is drawn; she is born from the lineage of Padmanarta.
The trident situated between the eyebrows has a body that is dark greenish-yellow, and it is constantly manifested from the Vajra family.
[133] Kinī;
she by whom a trident is seen on the forehead, and indeed a spear as well.
She has red eyes, is fair-skinned and red, and likewise has red hands and feet;
she always delights in goats or even cocks when they are consecrated. The sign of her presence in the house is a thunderbolt, which is likewise constantly worshipped there.
There is no doubt that these ḍākinīs have arisen from the family of Śrī Heruka.
She whose wheel (*cakra*) is seen on her forehead and also on her hand,
who is dark-complexioned like clarified butter or urine, and who always wears a *paṭṭa* on her forehead.
Endowed with great good fortune, virtuous, and supreme—
she in whose house the drawn mandala is always worshipped;
born from the family of Vajravārāhī, she is a ḍākinī proud of her power.
She who is dark like black collyrium, whose teeth are uneven,
who is cruel and constantly perverse, yet who is endowed with goodness;
she who is always fond of bathing, and who does not speak excessively with her words.
The auspicious vajra, when drawn, is constantly worshipped.
Born from the family of Vajravārāhī are fifteen thousand [deities]:
Gaurī, who resembles gold, as well as Ārukṣī and Lomasā.
She on whose forehead or hand a thunderbolt is seen is always established in sovereignty; she is pregnant and speaks the truth,
possessing a fragrance like that of jasmine.
In whose house the great Vajra is constantly worshipped,
there dwells the supreme Mahāyogīśvarī born of the Khaṇḍarohā lineage;
she who is eternally fond of meat, emaciated, and possesses the luster of black collyrium.
She who has a trident-mark on the edge of her forehead, who is devoted to the performance of harsh deeds,
who always dwells in cremation grounds, and who is fearless and pitiless—
she whose forehead is marked with a trident and a skull is worshipped in the home.
The ḍākinī of the god Śrī Heruka is born of that family;
she is a woman whose form is like a cloud, who possesses uneven teeth,
who is constantly engaged in cruel deeds, and whose left fangs are formidable.
She in whose house an axe is kept and constantly worshipped is a ḍākinī born from the lineage of Vināyaka; of this there is no doubt.
This description of the qualities arising from Heruka and his host of ḍākinīs has been proclaimed for the benefit of practitioners.
The thirty-seventh chapter on the characteristics of the ḍākinīs in the Abhidhānottara.
[1336] (End of the folio)
